name: Vacuum Cleaner Filter
definition: A vacuum-cleaner filter profile covers filtration position, media, sealing, class or test claims, pressure-drop and service boundaries; it does not make similarly shaped filters interchangeable across appliance models.
includedScope: Pre-motor, main, cartridge, flat-pleated and exhaust filter roles
Official particle-class and efficiency claims with their stated test boundary
Part-number, model, seal, dimension and wet/dry checks
excludedScope: Dust bags as universal substitutes for filters
headline: HEPA wording, color and shape are not enough—the exact part, filter position, seal and test boundary must match.
description: This profile separates filter function, filtration claims, airflow restrictions and model-specific compatibility so buyers can compare evidence without converting a class label into universal fit.
metaDescription: Vacuum cleaner filter types, HEPA classes, filter positions, pressure-drop and wet/dry boundaries, official part families and compatibility checks.
disclaimer: Physical resemblance, matching wattage, matching voltage, a generic family name or a seller claim does not establish compatibility. Verify the current manufacturer part number and revision, machine model and serial scope, electrical and control specification, mechanical and fluid or airflow interfaces, protection requirements and approved service documentation.

keyFacts.label: System role
keyFacts.value: A vacuum may use multiple filters in different positions
keyFacts.evidence: Miele describes an AirClean system with dustbag, motor-protection filter and exhaust filter.

keyFacts.label: Claim boundary
keyFacts.value: HEPA class and percentage claims require the stated method and product configuration
keyFacts.evidence: Kärcher publishes an H14 glass-fibre filter and a 99.995% claim for a named accessory; Miele references EN 1822:2019 for named products.
keyFacts.scope: Named manufacturer products and their stated tests only.

keyFacts.label: Compatibility boundary
keyFacts.value: Part number and appliance model remain primary identifiers
keyFacts.evidence: Dyson and Nilfisk list filters against specific vacuum models or ranges.

systemRole.name: Pre-separation
systemRole.role: Cyclones, bags or upstream stages remove part of the load before fine filtration.
systemRole.evidence: Miele describes the bag as one stage in a multi-stage system.

systemRole.name: Motor protection
systemRole.role: An upstream filter reduces particle exposure at the motor inlet.
systemRole.evidence: Miele explicitly identifies a motor-protection filter within its system.

systemRole.name: Main or cartridge filtration
systemRole.role: Pleated or cartridge media separates particles while maintaining the designed airflow path.
systemRole.evidence: Kärcher separates cartridge and flat-pleated families by application and material.

systemRole.name: Exhaust filtration
systemRole.role: A downstream filter addresses particles remaining in discharged air within the stated class and seal boundary.
systemRole.evidence: Dyson, Miele and Nilfisk publish model-specific post-motor or HEPA accessories.

architectures.name: Cartridge or cylindrical filter
architectures.operatingPrinciple: Pleated media is formed around a supporting core and sealed into a model-specific frame.
architectures.applicationBoundary: Common in wet/dry and cartridge-based vacuum designs.
benefits: Large media area in a compact envelope
architectures.buyerCheck: Match exact accessory number, media, dimensions, seals and wet/dry declaration.
architectures.evidence: Kärcher publishes cartridge and wet/dry product groups with distinct uses.

architectures.name: Flat-pleated filter
architectures.operatingPrinciple: Pleated media is packaged in a flat frame or cassette.
architectures.applicationBoundary: Kärcher separates Safety/HEPA, Ultimate, Wet & Dry and Dry families.
limitations: Color does not prove media or fit
architectures.buyerCheck: Verify part number, dust class, media, filter position and machine list.
architectures.evidence: Kärcher official filter overview separates four flat-pleated categories.

architectures.name: Pre-motor and exhaust pair
architectures.operatingPrinciple: Separate upstream and downstream filters protect the motor and manage discharged particles.
architectures.applicationBoundary: Cordless and canister systems may use distinct filter positions and part numbers.
benefits: Different functions can be optimized separately
Service intervals can be documented by position
limitations: Filters may look similar while serving different positions
Omitting one stage changes system performance
architectures.buyerCheck: Confirm every required filter position and exact appliance model.
architectures.evidence: Dyson and Miele publish model-specific filter and system guidance.

specifications.name: Filter position
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Defines whether the part protects the motor, performs main separation or filters exhaust
specifications.comparisonCaution: Do not substitute an exhaust filter for a pre-motor part.
specifications.evidence: Official sources publish this field or the related product boundary for named families.
specifications.scope: Use the exact source and current model documentation; field labels and test points vary by manufacturer.

specifications.name: Filtration class or efficiency
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Describes a result under a named standard or manufacturer method
specifications.reportingBoundary: Class, particle size, percentage, method and configuration must stay together
specifications.comparisonCaution: Do not compare percentages with missing test boundaries.
specifications.evidence: Official sources publish this field or the related product boundary for named families.
specifications.scope: Use the exact source and current model documentation; field labels and test points vary by manufacturer.

specifications.name: Pressure drop
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Influences airflow, motor load and service indicators
specifications.reportingBoundary: Report at the stated airflow and loading condition
specifications.comparisonCaution: Higher filtration wording does not automatically mean better system performance.
specifications.evidence: Official sources publish this field or the related product boundary for named families.
specifications.scope: Use the exact source and current model documentation; field labels and test points vary by manufacturer.

specifications.name: Media and wet/dry use
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Controls moisture tolerance, cleaning method and application
specifications.reportingBoundary: Paper, fleece, glass fibre and other media need exact manufacturer guidance
specifications.comparisonCaution: Do not wash or wet a filter unless explicitly permitted.
specifications.evidence: Official sources publish this field or the related product boundary for named families.
specifications.scope: Use the exact source and current model documentation; field labels and test points vary by manufacturer.

specifications.name: Seal and dimensions
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Define bypass leakage and physical installation
specifications.reportingBoundary: Frame, gasket, latch and orientation are compatibility fields
specifications.comparisonCaution: A small seal gap can invalidate a filtration claim.
specifications.evidence: Official sources publish this field or the related product boundary for named families.
specifications.scope: Use the exact source and current model documentation; field labels and test points vary by manufacturer.

specifications.name: Service interval
specifications.reportingBoundary: Wash, dry, replace and alarm instructions are model-specific
specifications.comparisonCaution: Do not reuse until the manufacturer-stated dry condition is met.
specifications.evidence: Official sources publish this field or the related product boundary for named families.
specifications.scope: Use the exact source and current model documentation; field labels and test points vary by manufacturer.
